prompt: A university's energy costs rose 25% in a year, while energy prices rose 10%. It opened two new buildings. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Higher energy prices likely explain most of the increase.
options.feedback: Prices rose 10% but costs rose 25%, so usage rose about 14%.

options.text: The two new buildings likely use much of the extra energy.
options.feedback: Right. Usage rose about 14% beyond prices, and two buildings opened. I'd compare energy use per square foot by building.

options.text: The new buildings are inefficient and need to be retrofitted.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain and jumps to an expensive fix before any data.

options.text: Students are probably using less energy in the old buildings.
options.feedback: That would lower costs, not raise them 25%.

explanation: The data shows energy costs up 25% against 10% for prices, so usage rose about 14% (1.25 ÷ 1.10) in the year two buildings opened. Likely cause: the new buildings use much of the extra energy. To test it, compare energy use per square foot by building. If use rose in the old buildings too, look at weather or equipment.
